walkthroughs.body_html:
Normal blood glucose ≈ 5 mmol/dm³.

After eating, glucose rises. Pancreas releases insulin, telling liver and muscle cells to store glucose as glycogen.

If glucose falls, pancreas releases glucagon, which breaks glycogen back into glucose.

Type 1 — insulin must be injected. Dose depends on carbohydrate eaten.

Example: 1 unit per 10 g carbs. Meal with 60 g carbs needs 6 units.

BMI = mass ÷ height². For 70 kg, 1.75 m: 70 ÷ (1.75 × 1.75) = 70 ÷ 3.0625 ≈ 22.9.

BMI 25+ is overweight — risk factor for type 2 diabetes.

mcqs.q: What does insulin do to blood glucose?
options: Sweating removes excess heat by carrying it out as liquid waste.
Insulin raises blood glucose to give the body energy.
Insulin destroys glucose in the bloodstream so it cannot be used.
It lowers blood glucose by causing cells (especially liver and muscle) to take it up and store it as glycogen.

mcqs.q: What does negative feedback do in homeostasis?
options: Negative feedback makes a process get worse or amplifies the change.
It reverses a change in a controlled variable, bringing it back towards the set point.
Negative feedback stops the body from responding to any internal change.
Insulin destroys glucose in the bloodstream so it cannot be used.

mcqs.q: How does sweating help cool you down?
options: Evaporation of sweat absorbs energy (latent heat) from the skin, lowering body temperature.
Sweat is cold and directly cools the skin on contact.
Negative feedback stops the body from responding to any internal change.
Sweating removes excess heat by carrying it out as liquid waste.
